extracted.intended_audience: applicants for suitability determinations, registered apprenticeship program sponsors, State Apprenticeship Agencies (SAAs), labor organizations, and other apprenticeship stakeholders submitting comments to the NPRM
extracted.subtask_description: Extracts standards and transition requirements in the Department of Labor's proposed rule for determining occupations' suitability for registered apprenticeship and for bringing programs/SAAs into compliance. Focuses on criteria (hours, instruction), timelines, roles, review processes, and requested commenter input.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposed transition timeline for §29.7 (occupations' suitability)
rubrics_metrics.description: Three scenarios with distinct timelines for when proposed §29.7 would apply: (1) Potential occupations—occupations not determined suitable prior to the effective date: 90 days following the effective date of the final rule. (2) Existing suitable occupations—occupations deemed suitable by the Administrator prior to the effective date: 4 years following the effective date. (3) SAA-approved occupations—occupations deemed suitable by an SAA prior to the effective date: 4 years following the effective date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Department organized transition provisions around these categories to promote clarity. The 90-day period allows OA to implement the updated process while accommodating applications in process; the 4-year period recognizes the significant undertaking to review previously approved occupations. The Department invites comments on necessity, length, feasibility, impacts to sponsors, and alternatives (e.g., permanent exemptions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposed transition timeline for Subpart A (§§29.8–29.23) (program standards)
rubrics_metrics.description: Timelines for program compliance with updated Subpart A: (1) Potential programs—new programs not previously registered by the Administrator: effective date of the final rule or when OA makes available an electronic submission process. (2) Existing registered apprenticeship programs—previously registered by the Administrator: 2 years following the effective date. (3) SAA-approved registered apprenticeship programs—programs previously registered by an SAA: 2 years following the SAA coming into compliance with the final rule; programs approved by SAAs after the effective date remain provisional until the SAA determines them in compliance with its approved State Apprenticeship Plan.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Paragraph (b) proposes immediate effectiveness for potential programs once an electronic submission process is available so OA can provide technical assistance. Paragraph (c) provides 2 years for established programs to update program standards, apprenticeship agreements, and other elements. The Department requests comments on sufficiency of these periods and feasibility for sponsors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposed transition provisions for SAAs, SAA-approved occupations, and SAA-registered apprenticeship programs
rubrics_metrics.description: Scenarios/timelines for State Apprenticeship Agencies: (1) Potential SAAs not previously recognized: effective date—must comply with §29.27 to receive recognition. (2) SAAs previously recognized by the Administrator: must come into full compliance with proposed §29.27 by December 31, 2026. (3) SAA-approved registered apprenticeship programs: 2 years following the SAA coming into compliance (approval of a State Apprenticeship Plan). (4) SAA-approved occupations: 4 years following the effective date of the final rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Department anticipates States may need to change apprenticeship-related laws; the December 31, 2026 date is intended to provide sufficient time. Paragraph (d)(1) requires SAAs to ensure programs registered prior to State Plan approval become consistent with the approved Plan within 2 years. The Department seeks comments on timing, implementation challenges, and impacts on recognition/status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Occupational suitability criteria (current 29 CFR 29.4 baseline)
rubrics_metrics.description: Under the current regulatory framework, an occupation is considered suitable for registered apprenticeship training if it meets four distinct criteria (current 29 CFR 29.4): (1) involve job skills customarily acquired through on-the-job training; (2) be 'clearly identifiable and recognizable' in an industry; (3) involve the progressive acquisition of skills and knowledge which would require at least 2,000 hours of on-the-job training; and (4) require related instruction in addition to the on-the-job training component.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department retains these four core factors as the foundation for suitability determinations and uses them to frame proposed §29.7. Comments and data are solicited on how these criteria operate in different industries and whether adjustments are needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum duration requirement: at least 2,000 hours of on-the-job training
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department proposes to retain the existing requirement that occupations must involve ‘at least 2,000 hours’ of on-the-job training—approximately 1 year of full-time work—as a minimum duration requirement for an occupation to be suitable for registered apprenticeship training.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department views the 2,000-hour minimum as a hallmark of quality to ensure occupational proficiency, adequate safety training, and supervised competency acquisition. Examples and rationale are provided (e.g., electrician programs often require 8,000 hours). The Department invites public comment and data on whether the 2,000-hour minimum is appropriate or should be changed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum related instruction requirement: at least 144 hours per 2,000 on-the-job hours
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed §29.7(b)(4) would require that an occupation's proposed work process schedule include at least 144 hours of related instruction, on average, per 2,000 hours of on-the-job training for the Department to determine suitability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is proposed as a uniform minimum (rather than a recommendation). Examples given: a 4,000-hour OJT submission would need 288 related instruction hours; a 3,000-hour program would be required to provide at least 144 related instruction hours because the requirement is applied at 2,000-hour intervals. The Department explains the 144-hour standard (e.g., 4 hours/week × 36 weeks) and its practical implications for older apprentices who balance work/life obligations. The Department requests comments on alternatives (e.g., minimum ratio applied to total hours, scaling methods) and on inclusion of instruction hours in the suitability determination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrator-exclusive authority for federal suitability determinations
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed §29.7(a)(2) would implement a requirement that occupations may only be determined suitable by the Administrator; SAAs that make apprenticeability determinations under current §§29.4 and 29.13 would not be able to make suitability determinations under proposed §29.7 for Federal purposes upon the effective date of the proposed rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This centralizes the federal suitability decision with OA. The NPRM explains the change and seeks comments, particularly from SAAs, on impacts and the process for transitioning SAA-approved occupations into Administrator determinations.

rubrics_metrics.name: 5-year periodic review process for suitable occupations (§29.7(h))
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed §29.7(h) would provide for an ongoing 5-year review process by OA of suitable occupations, work process schedules, and related instruction outlines to determine continued suitability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is proposed to allow OA to review previously approved occupations against updated criteria over time, reduce immediate burden on programs, and provide notice about timing of updates. The Department will develop technical assistance and seeks comments on the length and impact of the review cadence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program compliance responsibilities, timelines, and extension requests
rubrics_metrics.description: Program sponsors are ultimately responsible for their registered apprenticeship program's compliance with updated part 29. New (potential) programs must comply when an electronic submission process is available; existing registered programs must comply within 2 years of the final rule's effective date; SAA-registered programs must comply within 2 years after the SAA comes into compliance. The Department plans to permit requests for extensions of transition timelines for good cause.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department recognizes established programs may need longer transition time (e.g., to complete training cycles or rework work process schedules to meet 2,000-hour OJT requirement). The NPRM anticipates opportunities to request extensions and invites comments regarding feasibility, burdens on sponsors, and criteria for granting extensions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provision for applicants to submit occupational standards exceeding the minimums
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant submitting a suitability request may propose an occupation, work process schedule, and related instruction outline that exceeds the minimum standards to set an industry standard (e.g., submitting 8,000 OJT hours for an electrician).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposed §29.7(d) would solicit public comment to assist evaluation of such submissions. The Administrator may consider industry or occupational data (e.g., O*NET) and public comment when determining whether a submission meets or should exceed minimum requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of technical assistance and electronic submission tools to support transition
rubrics_metrics.description: OA plans to make available an electronic submission process and provide technical assistance to sponsors—such as boilerplate standards of apprenticeship, webinars, electronic tools, and other resources—concurrent with implementation of the updated requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Paragraph (b) ties the effective date for potential programs to availability of these tools. The Department asks for comments on whether the proposed supports and the timing of their availability are sufficient to facilitate compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of apprentice burdens and practical delivery of related instruction
rubrics_metrics.description: The NPRM notes that related instruction is often required during after-work hours and that the average U.S. apprentice is approximately 29 years old; increasing related instruction beyond 144 hours per 2,000 OJT could impose undue burden on apprentices balancing work and family obligations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This consideration informs the Department's proposal to retain a 144-hour related instruction minimum. The Department requests comments and evidence on the impact of instruction scheduling, costs (including whether sponsors reimburse instruction), and alternative approaches to balancing instructional quality with apprentice burden.
